issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s surrender that does not satisfy the required formalities does not terminate the tenancy, and the tenant may seek restoration of possession on the basis of the continuing tenancy.
material_facts: The tenant voluntarily handed possession of the land to the landlord.
The surrender was neither in writing nor verified through the required inquiry.
The landlord retained and personally cultivated the land, and the tenant sought restoration of possession.
issues.conclusion: The surrender was invalid and did not terminate the tenancy. The tenant remained entitled to possession and could claim restoration under the Act as a tenant.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 15, a surrender is valid only if it is in writing and verified by the Mamlatdar, who must ascertain that it is voluntary and not the result of pressure or undue influence. An invalid surrender is no surrender at all, so the tenancy continues; the tenant’s claim for possession is based on rights under the Act. Section 15(2) entitles the landlord to retain surrendered land only where the surrender complies with Section 15. Section 29(1), read with Sections 70(n) and 70(b), provides the procedure for restoring possession to a tenant entitled to it under the Act. Section 37’s express restoration provision does not imply that restoration is unavailable after an invalid surrender, because in that situation the tenancy was never terminated. The Court regarded Shankar Raoji v. Mahadu Govind, Durgaben v. Moria Bavia, and Trambaklal v. Shankerbhai as consistent with this interpretation.

rule.if: tenant_voluntarily_delivered_possession and surrender_formalities_missing and landlord_retained_possession and tenant_claimed_restoration_as_tenant

predicates.tenant_voluntarily_delivered_possession: The tenant voluntarily handed possession of the land to the landlord.
predicates.surrender_formalities_missing: The surrender was not made in writing and verified through the required procedure.
predicates.landlord_retained_possession: The landlord took and retained possession of the land after the surrender.
predicates.tenant_claimed_restoration_as_tenant: The tenant sought restoration of the land on the basis of the continuing tenancy.

issues.definition: When the tenant voluntarily delivered possession without the required surrender formalities, the landlord retained it, and the tenant sought restoration as a tenant, the tenant may recover possession through the tenant remedy.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who can seek restoration of possession through the ordinary tenant procedure cannot instead use the summary-eviction procedure against a landlord holding land after an invalid surrender.
material_facts: The tenant applied to the Collector for summary eviction of the landlord.
The landlord’s possession followed a surrender that did not comply with the required formalities.
The tenant’s tenancy continued, and the tenant could seek restoration from the Mamlatdar under the ordinary tenant procedure.
issues.conclusion: The Collector had no jurisdiction to entertain the summary-eviction application because the tenant’s remedy lay under Section 29(1), not Section 84.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29(1) permits a tenant entitled to possession under the Act to apply to the Mamlatdar, and Section 70(n) assigns the Mamlatdar the function of putting the tenant in possession under the Act. Section 84 is limited to the categories it specifies and, for the category applicable here, permits summary eviction only where the Act does not provide for eviction. The Legislature did not provide alternative remedies that would let a tenant bypass the Mamlatdar’s inquiry and the appeal available under Section 74. Shankar Raoji v. Mahadu Govind, Durgaben v. Moria Bavia, and Trambaklal v. Shankerbhai were consistent with this distinction between a claim for possession under the Act and summary eviction under Section 84.

predicates.tenant_filed_summary_eviction_applicatio: The tenant asked an administrative officer to summarily evict the person holding the land.
predicates.landlord_held_land_after_invalid_surrend: The landlord held the land after obtaining possession under a surrender that did not satisfy the required formalities.
predicates.tenant_restoration_remedy_available: The governing tenancy regime allowed the tenant to seek restoration through its ordinary tenant procedure.

issues.definition: If a tenant uses a summary-eviction proceeding against a landlord who holds land after an invalid surrender, and an ordinary tenant-restoration remedy is available, the summary-eviction officer lacks jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: Possession following an invalid surrender falls within the residual category of wrongful occupation, rather than the category concerning land acquired through an invalid transfer or acquisition.
material_facts: The landlord’s possession resulted from the tenant’s invalid surrender, not from a transfer or acquisition of land prohibited by the Act.
The land was not subject to management assumed under the Act.
The dispute concerned the tenant’s application to summarily evict the landlord.
issues.conclusion: The case fell under Section 84(c), not Section 84(a) or Section 84(b); the restriction applicable to that residual category therefore required that the Act provide no other remedy for eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 84(a) concerns land whose transfer or acquisition is invalid under the Act, which the Court read as referring to the restrictions on transfers and acquisitions in Chapter V, including Sections 63, 64 and 65. Section 84(b) concerns land whose management has been assumed under the Act. Possession following an invalid surrender falls instead under Section 84(c), which concerns land to whose use and occupation the person is not entitled and for which the Act provides no eviction remedy. The Court did not decide whether that no-other-remedy condition applies only to clause (c) or to all three clauses; it held that the case before it fell under clause (c).

predicates.tenant_filed_summary_eviction_applicatio: The tenant sought summary eviction of the person holding the land.
predicates.possession_followed_invalid_surrender: The person holding the land obtained possession following a surrender that did not satisfy the required formalities.
predicates.land_not_in_invalid_transfer_or_assumed_: The land was not held through a transfer or acquisition invalid under the governing regime, and its management had not been assumed under that regime.

issues.definition: When a summary-eviction proceeding concerns possession following an invalid surrender, and the land is outside the invalid-transfer and assumed-management categories, the possession falls in the residual wrongful-occupation category.
